correctness.rationale: For every Δ>0 the Gaussian integral produces a nonvanishing gauge factor times 1+2q cosh(w)+2q^4 cosh(2w). The exponential substitution yields a reciprocal quartic with nonzero constant, proving four zero multiplicities per period. The quadratic in y=cosh(w) has exactly two distinct discriminant roots in the physical parameter interval: s=1/2 and s=(sqrt(5)-1)/4. Q_q(±1) never vanishes; its negative-end minimum is positive. Continuity from s=1 and s=1/4 and the inverse-cosh geometry prove exactly the time-axis, rectangle, and half-time-line regimes, including both double-zero boundaries. The analytic chart z=ξ+ix supplies the sign and multiplicity of winding. Exact rational polynomial factorization and 2109 supplemental calculations were reproduced from the packaged checker; they are not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The smallest equal-amplitude symmetric harmonic comb with two outer frequency pairs is a canonical deterministic extension of current two-component interference models. Its four complex STFT phase singularities undergo two distinct sharp, exactly located collisions: time-axis pairs merge, form an off-axis rectangle, and re-emerge at half-time as separated spectral pairs. Complete location, multiplicity, winding and large-gap midpoint limits offer a concrete finite-parameter benchmark for phase-zero tracking and distinguish behavior not present in the elementary two-tone model. The precise two-transition topology, rather than mere numerical root computation, motivates the invariant; no general theorem or practical robustness claim is asserted.
